stopped_because: ran the 1 iterations it was given
policy_prompt_for_subgoal: Start in A: with the execution-start gripper empty, pick up the cube of the color named in the goal, pointing at its current visible center. Use only the execution scene for this pickup, not its earlier demonstration location. For every subgoal output, copy the menu label verbatim as the choice—'A', 'B', or 'C' for this menu—and supply any required [y, x] point separately. Never append the action description to the label. If the observed execution interval shows descent to that cube, closure to a grasp-sized opening (approximately 46%), and a lift with that opening maintained, choose B, dropping onto the goal-selected demonstration target stored in pre_press_target: the last completed target placement before the press for 'right before', or the first completed target placement after the press for 'right after'. Do not infer this temporal destination from the cube's current execution position. Explicit held-object evidence also permits B. The recorded cube coordinates may remain at the tabletop position after pickup and a held label may be absent; these do not override the closure-and-lift evidence. Match the remembered point to the corresponding visible target and point within that target, or use the remembered point if it is occluded. If pickup clearly closed on nothing or left the hand empty, choose A again at the requested cube. C is not required: the demonstration press identifies the desired target, and must not be reenacted. A completed release of the requested cube onto the selected target finishes the task; do not press the button afterward. For an otherwise unmatched nonterminal situation, choose B if there is credible evidence the requested cube is held, otherwise A at that cube. If pre_press_target is unknown and dropping is necessary, use the visible target nearest the requested cube as a deterministic fallback rather than asking for clarification.

fields.name: pre_press_target
fields.description: Despite its legacy name, this field holds the goal-selected demonstration target. When memory is empty and the demonstration is shown, locate the button press by closed-gripper descent onto the button and contact/depression, allowing temporary button occlusion. Read the temporal relation from the goal. For 'right before', find the instruction's cube's last completed target placement before the press. For 'right after', follow its next transfer and find its first completed target placement after the press; merely remaining on the old target immediately after button contact is not a new placement. Use release and subsequent resting evidence to identify the placement, allowing occlusion. Use the selected demonstration placement to identify the physical target, then follow that target through all subsequent demonstration frames to execution start, including shuffles, exchanges, crossings, and temporary occlusion. Resolve identity using the observed motion sequence and joint continuity of moving targets; do not assume spatial rank or target-list order identifies it, or independently match the final scene to its original position. Write exactly that physical target's reported execution-start center as [y, x], not its earlier demonstration center, the released cube's center, or the center of another target now occupying its former position. Ignore later placements when selecting the target, but continue tracking the selected target's subsequent motion. If its physical identity cannot be resolved, write "unknown". Once populated, copy the incoming value unchanged at every decision step; do not replace it with the cube's current position or a newly shifted visible centroid. If no target can be identified, write "unknown". e.g. [126, 145]
